metadata.scope: e_illyria (107 non-867 baronies across k_croatia, k_epirus, k_sicily, and k_venice; excludes baronies where is_historical_at['867'] is true)
metadata.hierarchy_note: hierarchy reflects data/ck3_title_tree.json (save-derived de jure tree including x_script_* dynamic titles); downstream localisation/historicity mods should key on barony_key and join against their target landed_titles tree.

schema_notes.vanilla_ck3_name: Exact English localisation string from CK3 titles_l_english.yml.
schema_notes.modern_name: Clean modern/standard English display name of the audited settlement or holding.
schema_notes.modern_name_note: Optional administrative parent, alternate designation, or native-script qualifier; null if none.
schema_notes.hierarchy: De jure title hierarchy from data/ck3_title_tree.json (empire, kingdom, duchy, county, holding_type).
schema_notes.is_historical_at: Bookmark-keyed booleans {'867', '1066', '1178'}; all entries here have '867': false.
schema_notes.replacement_candidates: List of exactly 3 associated natural feature names and historical tribal/ethnonym names (>=1 tribe per barony) usable as localisation replacements.
schema_notes.name: Clean display name of the replacement candidate (Wikipedia disambiguation suffixes extracted to disambiguation_note).
schema_notes.disambiguation_note: Optional disambiguator extracted from parenthetical/comma qualifiers (e.g. 'Liao', 'Orkney', 'river'); null if none.
schema_notes.localisation_stem: Clean CK3-ready toponym stem stripped of redundant generic English feature suffixes/prefixes ('River', 'Mount', 'Lake', 'people', etc.) while preserving meaningful compounds.
schema_notes.attestation_basis: Historicity classification distinguishing genuinely pre-867/pre-literate entities from medieval post-867 ethnogeneses: attested_pre_867 | indigenous_pre_literate | attested_867_to_1066 | attested_1066_to_1178.
schema_notes.valid_for_bookmarks: Bookmark-keyed booleans {'867', '1066', '1178'} indicating whether the replacement candidate is historically non-anachronistic for that bookmark (true for both attested_pre_867 and indigenous_pre_literate; bookmark-gated for attested_867_to_1066 and attested_1066_to_1178).
schema_notes.candidates_with_multilingual_variants: Count of replacement candidates having more than 1 distinct language_code (ISO 639-3 / ISO 639-5 or documented proto-stage code) across language_variants.
schema_notes.language_variants_policy: Include core local/classical forms plus regionally scoped vernaculars and genuinely distinct exonyms; exclude out-of-region exonym padding and redundant eng copies (eng is retained only when no non-English variant exists). Uses ISO 639-3 / ISO 639-5 language_code values plus documented Wiktionary proto/stage codes (sla-pro, gem-pro, cel-pro, cel-bry, urj-fin-pro); reconstructed proto/ancient forms carry a leading '*'.
schema_notes.language_variants: List of cultural/historical name forms: {form, native_script, language, language_code, notes}. form is always clean Latin script (or romanization) suitable for CK3 localisation; native_script holds the native non-Latin script form or null when the language natively uses Latin script.
schema_notes.relationship: Prose description of the geographical, ecological, or historical relationship between the replacement entity and the audited barony.
schema_notes.etymology_notes: Linguistic etymology, onomastic origin, or geographic/ethnographic characterization of the replacement entity (incorporating attested onomastic notes from language variants where documented).

replacement_candidates.name: Autariatae
replacement_candidates.relationship: Major Illyrian tribe inhabiting central and western Bosnia.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 4th century BCE (Pseudo-Scylax and classical Greek geographers)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Illyrian ethnonym, possibly connected to Proto-Indo-European *h2eus- or riverine roots.

replacement_candidates.name: Pliva
replacement_candidates.relationship: River joining the Vrbas at Jajce via the Pliva Waterfall.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 10th century CE (attested as Pliva župa in De Administrando Imperio)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Slavic hydronym derived from *pluti / *plivati ('to flow, swim').

replacement_candidates.name: Vrbas
replacement_candidates.relationship: Major river flowing directly past Jajce.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Attested as Urpanus in Pliny the Elder (Naturalis Historia, 77 CE).
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Ancient Illyrian hydronym later adapted in South Slavic via folk etymology with vrba ('willow').

replacement_candidates.name: Mazaei
replacement_candidates.relationship: Illyrian tribe of northwestern Bosnia along the Sana and Vrbas basins.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 1st century CE (9 CE during the Bellum Batonianum)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Illyrian ethnonym attested in Roman inscriptions and Strabo's Geographica.

replacement_candidates.name: Grmeč
replacement_candidates.relationship: Prominent mountain range rising west of Ključ na Sani.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Late medieval / early Ottoman-era toponym (c. 16th century CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: South Slavic oronym derived from grm ('oak, shrub').

replacement_candidates.name: Klekovača
replacement_candidates.relationship: High karst peak south of Ključ na Sani.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Early modern Bosnian oronym (pre-1700 CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: South Slavic oronym derived from kleka ('juniper').

replacement_candidates.name: Sardiatae
replacement_candidates.relationship: Illyrian tribe of western Bosnia.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 1st century CE (77 CE in Pliny the Elder's Naturalis Historia)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Illyrian tribal name recorded in Roman Dalmatian conventus lists.

replacement_candidates.name: Manjača
replacement_candidates.relationship: Karst mountain plateau overlooking the Vrbas gorge near Greben.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Early modern Dinaric oronym (pre-1700 CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Regional South Slavic oronym of the Dinaric karst.

replacement_candidates.name: Ugar
replacement_candidates.relationship: Right tributary of the Vrbas near Greben.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Medieval Bosnian hydronym (15th century CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Hydronym traditionally linked to medieval Hungarian (Ugar) presence or Slavic *ugor.

replacement_candidates.name: Daesitiates
replacement_candidates.relationship: Powerful Illyrian tribe of central Bosnia.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Attested in Roman accounts of the Bellum Batonianum (6–9 CE).
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Illyrian ethnonym recorded by Strabo, Velleius Paterculus, and Pliny.

replacement_candidates.name: Vrbanja
replacement_candidates.relationship: River flowing directly through Kotor Varoš.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Medieval Bosnian hydronym (14th century CE)

replacement_candidates.name: Vrbas
replacement_candidates.relationship: Major river of central Bosnia flowing past Kotor Varoš and Donji Kraji toward the Sava.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Attested as Urpanus in Pliny the Elder (Naturalis Historia, 77 CE).
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Classical Illyrian-Pannonian Urpanus, later Slavicized as Vrbas ('willow river').

replacement_candidates.name: Deuri
replacement_candidates.relationship: Illyrian tribe inhabiting the upper Vrbas and Pliva region.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 1st century CE (77 CE in Pliny the Elder's Naturalis Historia)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Illyrian ethnonym of the Dalmatian interior.

replacement_candidates.name: Vitorog
replacement_candidates.relationship: Mountain massif south of Sokol and Šipovo.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Early modern Dinaric oronym (pre-1700 CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: South Slavic compound meaning 'twisted horn', referring to the peak's shape.

replacement_candidates.name: Cincar
replacement_candidates.relationship: Mountain between Kupres and Livno bordering the Pliva-Vrbas divide.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Early modern Dinaric oronym (pre-1700 CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Linked to Aromanian (Tsintsar) pastoralists in the Dinaric highlands.

replacement_candidates.name: Iapodes
replacement_candidates.relationship: Illyrian-Celtic tribe centered in the Una river valley around Bihać.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Attested in Livy (for 171 BCE) and Strabo as inhabiting the karstic interior south of Carniola
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Ancient ethnonym of mixed Illyrian and Celtic peoples of Lika and Pounje.

replacement_candidates.name: Una
replacement_candidates.relationship: Major river flowing through Bihać.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 2nd century CE (attested in Roman sources as Oeneus)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Ancient Illyrian hydronym Oeneus, later reinterpreted in Latin as Una ('the one').

replacement_candidates.name: Plješevica
replacement_candidates.relationship: Mountain range forming the western border of the Bihać basin.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Early modern Dinaric oronym (pre-1700 CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: South Slavic oronym derived from plješiv ('bald, treeless summit').

replacement_candidates.name: Guduscani
replacement_candidates.relationship: Early medieval Slavic tribe of the Lika-Una borderlands.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 9th century CE (818 CE in the Royal Frankish Annals)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Slavic tribal name linked to the Gacka river or Gvozd.

replacement_candidates.name: Unac
replacement_candidates.relationship: Major tributary of the Una in western Bosnia.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Medieval Bosnian hydronym (15th century CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Diminutive of the Una river hydronym.

replacement_candidates.name: Korana
replacement_candidates.relationship: Karst river flowing north of the Una basin.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Medieval Croatian hydronym (13th century CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Pre-Slavic or Slavic hydronym, possibly from *kora ('bark, crust') or Illyrian root.

replacement_candidates.name: White Croats
replacement_candidates.relationship: Early Slavic people ancestral to the medieval Croatian realm including Pset.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Attested as Belochrobatoi in Constantine VII's De Administrando Imperio (c. 950 CE) and in the Primary Chronicle as an early medieval Slavic tribe of the Carpathian region.

replacement_candidates.name: Osječenica
replacement_candidates.relationship: Prominent mountain rising above the Pset/Petrovac plain.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Early modern Dinaric oronym (pre-1700 CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: South Slavic oronym from osječen ('cut off, steep-sided').

replacement_candidates.name: Šator
replacement_candidates.relationship: Karst mountain south of the Pset region.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Early modern Dinaric oronym (pre-1700 CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Derived from šator ('tent'), referring to its pyramidal peak.

replacement_candidates.name: Sclaveni
replacement_candidates.relationship: Early Slavic tribal confederation settling the Bosna valley.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 6th century CE (545 CE in Procopius's Wars)

replacement_candidates.name: Fojnička River
replacement_candidates.relationship: Left tributary of the Bosna river joining at Visoko.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 14th century CE (1365 CE in medieval Bosnian charters)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Medieval Bosnian hydronym of the central Bosna mining basin.

replacement_candidates.name: Bosna
replacement_candidates.relationship: Principal river of central Bosnia flowing past Visoko.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 1st century CE (9 CE as Bathinus flumen in Velleius Paterculus)

replacement_candidates.name: Ardiaei
replacement_candidates.relationship: Illyrian tribe of the upper Neretva and Rama highlands.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 4th century BCE (Greek historical accounts of Illyrian kingdoms)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Illyrian ethnonym, possibly linked to *ard- ('heron' or 'highland').

replacement_candidates.name: Neretva
replacement_candidates.relationship: Major river whose tributary system drains Prozor-Rama.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 4th century BCE (Pseudo-Scylax's Periplus as Naron)

replacement_candidates.name: Raduša
replacement_candidates.relationship: Mountain rising north of Prozor-Rama.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Early modern Dinaric oronym (pre-1700 CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: South Slavic oronym from personal name Raduš / rad ('glad').

replacement_candidates.name: Pannonian Avars
replacement_candidates.relationship: Early medieval nomadic confederation exerting rule over the Sava-Bosna corridor.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Attested in Byzantine and Latin sources from 558 CE onward, dominating the Pannonian frontier until Charlemagne's campaigns (791–796 CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Eurasian steppe ethnonym of contested Turkic/Mongolic origin.

replacement_candidates.name: Lašva
replacement_candidates.relationship: Major tributary of the Bosna river south of Vranduk.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 13th century CE (1244 CE in Bela IV's charter)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Medieval Bosnian hydronym, possibly pre-Slavic or from Slavic *lěska.

replacement_candidates.name: Vranica
replacement_candidates.relationship: Highest mountain range of central Bosnia southwest of Vranduk.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Late medieval Bosnian oronym (15th century CE)

replacement_candidates.name: Vlachs
replacement_candidates.relationship: Romance-speaking pastoralists attested throughout medieval central Bosnia.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Attested in 976 CE in Byzantine chronicler John Skylitzes and in 12th–13th century CE Hungarian charters.

replacement_candidates.name: Krivaja
replacement_candidates.relationship: Meandering tributary of the Bosna river north of Bobovac.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Indigenous Slavic hydronym of eastern Bosnia.

replacement_candidates.name: Zvijezda
replacement_candidates.relationship: Mountain ridge overlooking Vareš and Bobovac.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Early modern Bosnian oronym (pre-1700 CE)

replacement_candidates.name: Croats
replacement_candidates.relationship: South Slavic people inhabiting medieval western and central Bosnia.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Attested as Chrobati in the Charter of Duke Trpimir (852 CE) and De Administrando Imperio.

replacement_candidates.name: Lašva Valley
replacement_candidates.relationship: Fertile central Bosnian valley centered on Travnik.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 13th century CE (1244 CE as župa Lašva)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Named after the Lašva river flowing through the valley.

replacement_candidates.name: Čvrsnica
replacement_candidates.relationship: High Dinaric mountain massif south of central Bosnia.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Early modern Dinaric oronym (pre-1700 CE)

replacement_candidates.name: Serbs
replacement_candidates.relationship: South Slavic people attested in medieval eastern Bosnia and adjacent regions.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 9th century CE (822 CE in the Royal Frankish Annals)

replacement_candidates.name: Miljacka
replacement_candidates.relationship: River flowing directly through the Vrhbosna basin.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 15th century CE (1455 CE in early Ottoman defters)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: South Slavic hydronym linked to mil ('pleasant') or personal name Miljak.

replacement_candidates.name: Trebević
replacement_candidates.relationship: Mountain overlooking the Vrhbosna basin.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Early modern Bosnian oronym (pre-1700 CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Derived from Old Slavic *trebište ('sacrificial altar, clearing').

replacement_candidates.name: Ostrogoths
replacement_candidates.relationship: East Germanic people ruling Dalmatia and Bosnia in Late Antiquity.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 3rd century CE (291 CE in Latin panegyrics)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Germanic ethnonym meaning 'eastern Goths' or 'Goths of the rising sun'.

replacement_candidates.name: Krivaja
replacement_candidates.relationship: Major mountain river rising in the eastern Bosnian highlands near Olovo.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Indigenous Slavic hydronym of eastern Bosnia.

replacement_candidates.name: Jahorina
replacement_candidates.relationship: Major mountain massif in eastern Bosnia.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Early modern Bosnian oronym (pre-1700 CE)

replacement_candidates.name: Gepids
replacement_candidates.relationship: East Germanic people controlling Sirmium and the Drina-Sava frontier.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: First attested in a Latin panegyric of 291 CE; ruled the Tisza plain and Transylvania (Gepidia) from 454 to 567 CE.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: East Germanic ethnonym recorded by Jordanes and Procopius.

replacement_candidates.name: Drinjača
replacement_candidates.relationship: River flowing directly past the Kušlat fortress.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Medieval Bosnian hydronym (14th century CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Derivative of the Drina river hydronym.

replacement_candidates.name: Javor
replacement_candidates.relationship: Mountain massif in the Drinjača watershed.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Early modern Bosnian oronym (pre-1700 CE)

replacement_candidates.name: Dardani
replacement_candidates.relationship: Ancient Illyrian-Thracian tribe bordering the upper Drina.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 4th century BCE (classical Greek and Macedonian sources)

replacement_candidates.name: Drina
replacement_candidates.relationship: Major river flowing east of Srebrenica.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 1st century CE (attested in Strabo as Drilon / Roman Drinus)

replacement_candidates.name: Tara
replacement_candidates.relationship: Mountain massif across the Drina gorge from Srebrenica.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Medieval Balkan oronym (pre-1700 CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Traditionally linked to the Illyrian Autariatae ethnonym.

replacement_candidates.name: Autariatae
replacement_candidates.relationship: Ancient Illyrian tribe inhabiting upper Bosnia, the Tara/Drina/Neretva highlands, and eastern Herzegovina.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 4th century BCE (Pseudo-Scylax and classical Greek geographers)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Illyrian ethnonym associated with the Tara river valley.

replacement_candidates.name: Prača
replacement_candidates.relationship: River flowing south of Rogatica into the Drina.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Late medieval Bosnian hydronym (15th century CE)

replacement_candidates.name: Devetak
replacement_candidates.relationship: Karst mountain north of Rogatica.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Early modern Bosnian oronym (pre-1700 CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: South Slavic oronym derived from devet ('nine').

replacement_candidates.name: Liburnians
replacement_candidates.relationship: Ancient maritime tribe of the northern Adriatic coast and hinterland.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Attested by Pseudo-Scylax (4th century BCE, circa 350 BCE).
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Ancient Adriatic ethnonym of Liburnian/Illyrian origin.

replacement_candidates.name: Gacka
replacement_candidates.relationship: Karst sinking river south of Brinje.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 9th century CE (associated with the Guduscani in 818 CE)

replacement_candidates.name: Velebit
replacement_candidates.relationship: Largest mountain range of Croatia towering west of Brinje and Gacka.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 1st century CE (attested in Strabo as Albia / Albius)

replacement_candidates.name: Histri
replacement_candidates.relationship: Ancient tribe of Istria and the Kvarner Gulf.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Attested in Livy's account of the Roman conquest of Istria in 178–177 BCE.
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Ancient Indo-European ethnonym related to the Ister/Danube root.

replacement_candidates.name: Kvarner Gulf
replacement_candidates.relationship: Adriatic bay directly fronting Rijeka.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 1st century CE (77 CE as Sinus Flanaticus in Pliny)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Medieval Kvarner/Quarnaro derived from Latin Quaternarius.

replacement_candidates.name: Učka
replacement_candidates.relationship: Mountain range rising directly west of Rijeka.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Medieval Istrian oronym (12th century CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Derived from Slavic *vlъkъ ('wolf') or pre-Slavic root.

replacement_candidates.name: Iapodes
replacement_candidates.relationship: Illyrian-Celtic people inhabiting Lika, Gorski Kotar, and the Una valley in northwestern Bosnia.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Attested in Livy (for 171 BCE) and Strabo as inhabiting the karstic interior south of Carniola
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Ancient Adriatic-Dinaric ethnonym of mixed Illyrian-Celtic culture.

replacement_candidates.name: Lika
replacement_candidates.relationship: Sinking river flowing through the Lika plateau past Gospić.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 10th century CE (950 CE in De Administrando Imperio)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Linked to Greek λύκος ('wolf') or Illyrian/Slavic *lьka.

replacement_candidates.name: Albius Mons
replacement_candidates.relationship: Classical Roman name for the Dinaric karst chain dividing Lika and Liburnia from Pannonia.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Attested in Strabo (Geographica) as the western Dinaric karst range.

replacement_candidates.name: Dalmatae
replacement_candidates.relationship: Ancient Illyrian-Romanized population of the eastern Adriatic coast and Dinaric littoral.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Attested in Roman sources during the Dalmatian Wars (156 BCE).
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Ancient Illyrian tribe giving its name to Dalmatia.

replacement_candidates.name: Velebit Channel
replacement_candidates.relationship: Adriatic strait separating Karlobag from Pag Island.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Late medieval Venetian nautical charts (15th century CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Named after the Velebit mountain range and Morlach coast.

replacement_candidates.name: Pag
replacement_candidates.relationship: Adriatic island directly opposite Karlobag across the Velebit Channel.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 1st century CE (attested in Pliny as Cissa / medieval Pagus)

replacement_candidates.name: Catari
replacement_candidates.relationship: Illyrian tribe of the western Croatian and Pannonian borderlands.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 1st century CE (77 CE in Pliny the Elder's Naturalis Historia)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Illyrian/Pannonian ethnonym recorded in Roman sources.

replacement_candidates.name: Krbava
replacement_candidates.relationship: Karst polje and river basin directly below Udbina.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 10th century CE (950 CE as Kribasa in De Administrando Imperio)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Medieval Croatian toponym of pre-Slavic or Slavic origin.

replacement_candidates.name: Mala Kapela
replacement_candidates.relationship: Mountain range northeast of Krbava and Udbina.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Early modern Croatian oronym (pre-1700 CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Paired with Velika Kapela ('Little Chapel' pass).

replacement_candidates.name: Varciani
replacement_candidates.relationship: Pannonian-Illyrian tribe of the Kupa-Korana region.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 1st century CE (77 CE in Pliny the Elder's Naturalis Historia)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Pannonian ethnonym attested by Pliny and Ptolemy.

replacement_candidates.name: Plitvice Lakes
replacement_candidates.relationship: Karst lake system immediately south of Drežnik Grad.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Early modern Croatian hydronym (attested on 17th-century CE maps)

replacement_candidates.name: Mrežnica
replacement_candidates.relationship: Karst river flowing north of Drežnik Grad into the Korana.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Medieval Croatian hydronym (15th century CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Derived from Croatian mreža ('net', referring to travertine barriers).

replacement_candidates.name: Oseriates
replacement_candidates.relationship: Illyrian-Pannonian tribe of the Sava-Kupa basin.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Attested by Pliny the Elder (77 CE).
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Illyrian/Pannonian ethnonym, possibly linked to Slavic/IE *ezero ('lake').

replacement_candidates.name: Dobra
replacement_candidates.relationship: River flowing through the Modruš-Ogulin basin.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Medieval Croatian hydronym (14th century CE)

replacement_candidates.name: Klek
replacement_candidates.relationship: Iconic rocky peak overlooking Ogulin and Modruš.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Early modern Croatian oronym (pre-1700 CE)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: South Slavic oronym meaning 'steep crag' or 'juniper'.

replacement_candidates.name: Latobici
replacement_candidates.relationship: Celtic tribe inhabiting the lower Krka and Kupa-Sava borderlands.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Attested in Pliny the Elder's Naturalis Historia (77 CE) as dwelling in southwestern Pannonia Superior (Lower Carniola)
replacement_candidates.etymology_notes: Celtic ethnonym attested in Pannonia Superior.

replacement_candidates.name: Žumberak Mountains
replacement_candidates.relationship: Mountain range adjacent to Okić.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: Medieval Croatian-Slovene oronym (13th century CE)

replacement_candidates.name: Kupa
replacement_candidates.relationship: Major river flowing south of Okić.
replacement_candidates.earliest_attestation_note: 1st century CE (attested in Strabo and Pliny as Colapis)
